findings.description:
Command run: PYTHONPATH=packages/context-eval/src:packages/context-eval/tests python - <<'PY'
import json, tempfile
from copy import deepcopy
from pathlib import Path
from context_eval import enablement_gate, report as report_module
from context_eval.__main__ import main as cli_main
from context_eval.loader import load_corpus
import test_enablement_gate_mutation as t
root = Path.cwd()
tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='round3-body-miss-', dir='/tmp'))
corpus = load_corpus(t.CORPUS_ROOT)
base = t._document(corpus, t._measurement())
print('base_verdict', base['verdict'])
print('base_schema_errors', len(list(report_module.report_validator().iter_errors(base))))
print('base_body_consistency', report_module.body_consistency(base).consistent, report_module.body_consistency(base).derived_verdict, report_module.body_consistency(base).recorded_verdict)
for label, mutate in [('omit_gate', lambda d: d.__setitem__('gates', d['gates'][1:])), ('omit_case', lambda d: d.__setitem__('cases', d['cases'][1:])), ('omit_consumer', lambda d: d.__setitem__('per_consumer', d['per_consumer'][1:]))]:
    d = deepcopy(base)
    mutate(d)
    raw = tmp / f'{label}.json'
    raw.write_text(json.dumps(d), encoding='utf-8')
    schema_errors = list(report_module.report_validator().iter_errors(d))
    bc = report_module.body_consistency(d)
    check_exit = cli_main(['check', '--report', str(raw), '--corpus', str(t.CORPUS_ROOT)])
    check_digest_exit = cli_main(['check', '--report', str(raw), '--corpus', str(t.CORPUS_ROOT), '--verify-corpus-digest'])
    helper = t._helper_with_default(tmp / f'{label}-helper', enabled=True)
    cdir = tmp / f'{label}-contract'; cdir.mkdir()
    contract = t._contract(cdir, t._recorded_fingerprint(d))
    gate_exit = enablement_gate.main(['--repository-root', str(root), '--semantic-context', str(helper), '--report', str(raw), '--corpus', str(t.CORPUS_ROOT), '--embedding-contract', str(contract)])
    print(label, 'schema_errors', len(schema_errors), 'body_consistency', bc.consistent, bc.derived_verdict, bc.recorded_verdict, 'body_failures', list(bc.body_failures), 'check_exit', check_exit, 'check_digest_exit', check_digest_exit, 'gate_exit', gate_exit)
PY
Observed output excerpt: base_verdict pass
base_schema_errors 0
base_body_consistency True pass pass
omit_gate schema_errors 0 body_consistency True pass pass body_failures [] check_exit 0 check_digest_exit 0 gate_exit 3
omit_case schema_errors 0 body_consistency True pass pass body_failures [] check_exit 0 check_digest_exit 0 gate_exit 3
omit_consumer schema_errors 0 body_consistency True pass pass body_failures [] check_exit 0 check_digest_exit 0 gate_exit 3
The same command printed enablement-gate refusals naming report_describes_corpus for each mutant, so the enablement gate is protected, but context_eval check still exits 0 on schema-valid passing reports that omit a declared gate, case, or consumer. body_consistency therefore does not fully re-derive the composer pass invariant from the report body: compose_verdict can only produce pass after every declared case/gate/consumer row exists, while body_consistency only checks unscored rows and cases_scored vs cases_declared and never compares len(gates) to corpus.gates_declared, len(per_consumer) to corpus.consumers_declared, or len(cases) to corpus.cases_declared.
findings.resolution: Make context_eval check reject the same corpus-coverage contradictions the enablement gate rejects. Either move/report a public corpus-description helper and call it from _check, or extend body_consistency to fail a recorded pass when the body counts and row counts disagree (gates, consumers, cases, cases_scored) and have _check also verify declared ids against the loaded corpus.
